title: Monster Merchant
text: “There’s something called ‘Weapon Copy’ for the Hero’s weapons—”
My Father apologetically explained the concept of Weapon Copy to my dad. Well, it’s basically like openly admitting you’re a thief. It’s not exactly something you should be telling a shop owner.
“Huh… I see. I wondered what was going on when the Hero—other than Spear Hero—showed up first, touched the weapons, and seemed to be thinking about something. So that’s what he was up to.”
He’s nodding, looking a bit annoyed. I did that myself at first, too. I remember walking into the shop with my pig friends, laughing our heads off.

Since I knew Zeltoble’s inventory from my gaming knowledge, I remember telling my pig friends—loud enough for my dad to hear—that it was a lousy shop before we walked out. Of course, I made sure to copy the weapons first. That gave me quite a bit of breathing room. But when you think about it, it really is theft.
“It’s fine. You’ve been through a lot, An-chan, so don’t worry about it—go ahead and take a look at the shields. As long as the actual stock doesn’t decrease, I’m not losing anything.”
“Thank you…”
“Oh, wait a sec.”
The old man headed off to the back of the room. It looks like he’s rummaging through something on the second floor of the weapon shop. Meanwhile, Father gathered up all the shields from the shop.
“Found it, found it. Sorry to keep you waiting. This is a rare shield in this country.”
With that, the old man emerged from the back of the room carrying what looked like a meteorite shield sold in Zeltoble. A meteorite shield in a place like this!? That’s quite a surprise.
“What about you, An-chan, the spear-wielder?”
“I’m fine. I already have that type of weapon.”
“Is that so?”

It really is true that the answer lies right under your nose… To be honest, back when I was chasing pigs, I thought this shop was just an ordinary one. I assumed Father favored it because it had helped him out during tough times, but it turns out the owner’s craftsmanship is truly exceptional.

…I remember how Father used to display the shield the shop owner made with great care in the village warehouse. He’d polish it regularly and treat it like a treasure. I used a replica of that shield back then, and it seems it was quite an exceptional piece. I’ve heard that the sword Ren used was actually the one the owner of this armory had used himself.

He’s definitely skilled. On the other hand, what was I using? I was using a replica of the spear that Big Sister’s older sister found on the ocean floor. As a result of borrowing it temporarily, I learned Skills that evolved into “Brionac.” If I get the chance, I’ll have him make one for me, too.
“Go ahead and copy this while you’re at it. It’s a shield made from a rare ore that fell from the sky. It’s a display item from Zeltoble—a prototype from the Meteorite series.”
“Meteorite… Motoyasu-kun, is this rare?”
“You probably can’t copy it unless you go all the way to Zeltoble. And the Skills you can learn from it are pretty impressive.”
“I see… Thank you so much for everything.”
“Don’t worry about it. If you’d like, please support my shop.”
“Yeah. I definitely will… I’ll be back.”
“Don’t be so shy, An-chan. That’s more like you—a little cocky, right?”
At Father’s words, Father slowly gripped the meteorite shield and handed it back.
“You’re right… I’ll be back, so look forward to it!　I’m going to use the money I earn to have Father make me some great gear!”

Father, who had been keeping a low profile, closed his eyes for a moment before answering cheerfully. That’s right. Father was actually a pretty lively guy by nature. During the last loop, he was reserved and had a gentle demeanor.

The gunsmith’s interpersonal skills—which brought out Father’s true personality—are truly commendable. I’d like to be on such good terms with my Father that he can call me by my first name without hesitation, too.
“Keep it up, An-chan. Alright, go on then!”
“Yeah! See you later!”
“Well then, goodbye.”
And so we left the weapon shop. By the way, Yuki-chan and the others were chirping away, trying to squeeze into the gaps in my Father’s armor.
“So, shall we go buy a slave next? Or should Motoyasu-kun go level up Yuki-chan and the others?”
“That’s true…”
It’s not like there’s no way to level up in secret. But considering the hassle, picking out a slave isn’t a bad idea.
“Then let’s go buy a slave.”
“U-un…”

My father nods, swallowing hard, and follows me. I wonder what’s going on? If I had to describe it, the atmosphere is like he’s mustering up the courage to enter a nightclub with a friend for the first time.

However, as I’ve thought many times before, whenever I walk through the town of Melromarc with my father, we attract a lot of suspicious stares. I do find myself thinking, “Should I just slaughter them all?” but of course, I mustn’t do that.
We made our way through the back alleys toward the monster merchant’s tent. In front of the tent, Father tapped me on the shoulder and asked:
“A-are they selling slaves here?”
“That’s right. They also sell monsters.”
“H-huh… If the goal is just to get stronger, using monsters isn’t a bad idea, is it?”
“I wouldn’t really recommend it.”

Our goal this time is to buy a slave to work as a salesperson. If we’re going to use monsters for power-leveling, it’s no different from doing it with Filolial-sama. I suppose my Father is hesitant about buying a slave.
“Well then, let’s go.”
“Yeah.”
When we stepped inside the tent, the monster merchant was there as usual. Still, this guy is dressed in a strange way. He looks like he’s running a one-man circus.
Huh!? The Filolial Circus! My imagination is running wild. What a wonderful dream. Once the Filolial Ranch is complete, let’s all give it a try.
“Well, well, a new customer, I see? Hello.”
“Filo-tan.”
“Huh?”
“Motoyasu, what are you suddenly talking about? Filo-tan is my future adopted child, right? What’s going on?”
Oh? I blurted out “Filo-tan” without thinking. Didn’t we decide to put off the search for Filo-tan for now?
“My mistake.”
“Judging by that appearance… and the weapons you’re carrying, you must be the Spear Heroes and Shield Heroes, correct?”
My father is glaring at the monster merchant with a stern expression. He looks as if he’s worried that admitting it here might put him at a disadvantage.
“Rest assured, we adjust our prices after assessing our customers. Yes.”
“…I see.”
My Father, his guard slightly lowered, took a step forward.
“Oh? You’re the Shield Hero, aren’t you? Yes. Judging by the aura you give off, it seems you have no business at our shop, doesn’t it?”
“…Sorry, but I can’t just let you look down on me like that.”
Muttering that under his breath, Father took a deep breath before speaking up. He’s quite skilled at business, after all. I can watch from the sidelines with peace of mind.
“Judging people? The only reason you can say something like that is because you’re completely looking down on me.”
“No, no. Everyone has a certain level of generosity. Yes. Our livelihood is providing for those who desire it. Yes.”
“So, does that mean you’re dividing your offerings into those for wealthy nobles and those for poor nobles?”
“That’s generally correct. Yes.”
“Well… fine. Then show me the goods for the wealthy. We’ll negotiate later. Of course, don’t think you can fudge the market price.”
At Father’s words, the monster merchant grinned.
“Here you are. Yes.”
My father scanned the list of slaves at the back of the tent.
“There are a lot of Demi-Humans here, aren’t there?”
“Since Melromarc is a country that prioritizes humans, it’s difficult to trade in humans. Yes.”
“That’s true. You have to go a little deeper to find any.”

He’s clenching his wrist tightly—it looks like he’s trying to suppress his trembling. Are there human slaves in this country? That’s news to me. As expected of Father—he’s truly well-informed. Hmm? Why does Father even know such a thing in the first place?
“So? How much is this slave?”
Pointing slowly at a slave in a cage, Father asked.
“As for this slave—”
He continued talking with the monster merchant. Eventually, he went on to look at the slaves meant for the poor as well.
“I get the general idea.”
Then, after falling deep in thought, my Father muttered,
“It’s quite a bit higher than the going rate, isn’t it?”
Oh? My Father shouldn’t have seen where the other slaves were being sold, should he? What on earth does this mean?
